item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","shard_id":"8B-S03","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0015-E013","BATCH-0015-E014","BATCH-0015-E015","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0015-E019","BATCH-0016-E001","BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0016-E009","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E011","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0016-E015","BATCH-0016-E016","BATCH-0016-E017","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0017-E001","BATCH-0017-E002","BATCH-0017-E003","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0017-E008","BATCH-0017-E009","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E007","BATCH-0018-E011","BATCH-0018-E012","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0018-E014","BATCH-0018-E015"],"answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shard documents a partly explicit program: pacification through addressing social causes, employment, welfare, reconciliation, and rejection of a frontal war, alongside formal plans for security, justice, social policy, development, labor, energy, and infrastructure. It also records a divergence between the stated pacification and social-cause program and the subsequent emphasis on militarization. Some broader economic and institutional agendas are attributed to the administration but not always to López Obrador personally.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E001","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0017-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a complete dated portfolio of all presidential goals or establish which formally stated goals were personally owned by the ruler.","The security report is evaluative and some economic agendas are institutional rather than personal presidential commitments."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"There is substantial evidence of translation into laws, budgets, institutions, and administrative machinery, including creation and expansion of the Guardia Nacional, military-security legislation, labor and pension reforms, tax-administration changes, fiscal measures, and formal programs. However, implementation was frequently under-specified, technically weak, or inconsistent with stated aims; several proposed fiscal reforms remained prospective.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E001","BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0017-E003","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0017-E008","BATCH-0017-E009","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E012","BATCH-0018-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E015","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0017-E001","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0018-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The evidence does not establish that every enacted measure was personally directed by López Obrador.","Some measures and effects are projected, institutionally diffuse, or evaluated only through secondary and advocacy sources."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"Executed resources show strong mobilization toward military security: military institutions received most security spending, military staffing expanded, and the Guardia Nacional grew materially. Other mobilization included tax administration, social programs, labor institutions, refugee administration, and emergency coordination. Yet local police and justice capacity were comparatively weakened, and the Guardia Nacional’s activity did not match its budgetary and rhetorical prominence.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E007","BATCH-0018-E014","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0018-E004"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Spending and staffing demonstrate mobilization but not by themselves effective execution of the full program.","Several initiatives relied heavily on UN, civil-society, state, municipal, or external support."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The shard shows some staffing and capacity-building, including expanded COMAR personnel, trained public servants, strengthened labor and victim-protection capacities, and new or expanded institutional personnel. It also documents serious appointment and personnel-management weaknesses: delayed high-level appointments, impaired institutional quorum, military dominance in security staffing, inadequate staffing ratios, and concerns about personnel capability and training.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0018-E014","BATCH-0018-E015","BATCH-0015-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0018-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard rarely identifies individual presidential appointment decisions or evaluates the competence of particular appointees.","Some staffing evidence concerns subnational or partner institutions rather than the presidential chain of command."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination was observable in selected programs: interagency labor, refugee, development, and emergency mechanisms operated across federal, state, municipal, UN, and civil-society actors. However, coordination and territorial control were uneven. Evidence includes severe implementation divergence across states, incomplete service coverage, weak local capacity, appointment-related institutional dysfunction, and the Culiacán operation’s intelligence, extraction, and territorial-control failures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E014","BATCH-0015-E015","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0017-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0015-E019","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0018-E007","BATCH-0018-E014","BATCH-0018-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Many favorable coordination findings describe UN-led or partner-led coordination and do not isolate presidential control.","The shard does not provide a comprehensive national compliance or milestone record."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"The shard records numerous observable implementations: labor-contract review, employment and refugee-integration programs, tax-administration reforms, social transfers, pension changes, emergency operations, institutional digitization, laws, budgets, and infrastructure initiatives. It also records substantial gaps between formal action and practice, including ineffective migrant-child protection, weak victim services, underperforming security institutions, inadequate justice enforcement, unclear program rules, and persistent anti-corruption failures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E013","BATCH-0015-E014","BATCH-0015-E015","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E007","BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0017-E008","BATCH-0017-E009","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E007","BATCH-0018-E011","BATCH-0018-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Implementation evidence is heterogeneous and often program-specific rather than nationally representative.","Some adverse findings are advocacy or evaluative judgments, while favorable records may reflect official or partner reporting."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Results are mixed and goal-specific. Some indicators moved toward stated goals, including reductions in homicide, several urban crimes, insecurity perceptions, inflation pressures, labor income, tax revenue performance, and selected inclusion or integration outcomes. Other indicators moved adversely or remained unresolved: violence and disappearances remained high, justice-system impunity and backlogs worsened, Guardia Nacional activity was not associated consistently with homicide reduction, regional inequality persisted, and several outcomes had attribution or measurement problems.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E013","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0016-E009","BATCH-0017-E002","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0017-E008","BATCH-0017-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0015-E019","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E008","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E011","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0016-E017","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0017-E001","BATCH-0017-E006","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several favorable outcomes are self-reported, partner-attributed, projected, or confounded by external shocks and inherited trends.","The homicide decline is subject to classification and undercounting concerns, and the shard does not establish a complete counterfactual."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"There is evidence of some adaptation: digital transformation of refugee administration, expansion of emergency and coordination mechanisms, subsidy tapering when market pressures abated, and institutional learning or capacity-building in selected programs. But the shard also records weak or absent correction: repeated implementation failures, unresolved migrant-child and disaster-response gaps, persistent anti-corruption deficiencies, continued militarization despite adverse evidence, denial or dismissal of surveillance allegations, and limited response to justice and appointment failures.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0015-E018","BATCH-0017-E003","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0017-E008","BATCH-0018-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E007","BATCH-0015-E019","BATCH-0016-E003","BATCH-0016-E021","BATCH-0016-E022","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E006","BATCH-0018-E007","BATCH-0018-E011","BATCH-0018-E013","BATCH-0018-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard contains few direct records linking audits or evaluations to ruler-directed replacement, reallocation, or course correction.","Some apparent adaptation was undertaken by autonomous agencies or external partners rather than the president."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"Crisis responses were mixed. Favorable evidence includes rapid local displacement response, coordinated Hurricane Otis structures, inflation management through monetary and fiscal measures, and refugee-system expansion that helped avoid collapse. Adverse evidence includes the failed Culiacán operation and release of the target, weak disaster follow-up and transparency, continuation of militarization despite legal and rights concerns, and responses to surveillance disclosures that allegedly denied or obscured the issue.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E015","BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0015-E017","BATCH-0017-E001","BATCH-0017-E002","BATCH-0018-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E004","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E012","BATCH-0018-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several crisis responses were substantially supported or coordinated by external actors.","The Culiacán account relies partly on cited press reporting, and disaster-response evidence does not fully assess recovery or distributional outcomes."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the period end, the shard shows durable institutional and policy changes, including the Guardia Nacional and expanded military role, labor and pension reforms, tax-administration structures, refugee-system digitization, and selected infrastructure and social programs. It also documents fragility or regression in justice capacity, local security institutions, victim protection, anti-corruption enforcement, disaster preparedness, and violence outcomes. The end-period record is therefore substantively mixed, with durability stronger for some administrative and military arrangements than for the stated pacification, justice, and rights-related objectives.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0015-E016","BATCH-0016-E002","BATCH-0016-E010","BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0017-E005","BATCH-0017-E007","BATCH-0017-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E012","BATCH-0018-E001","BATCH-0018-E004","BATCH-0018-E005","BATCH-0018-E010","BATCH-0018-E011","BATCH-0018-E012","BATCH-0018-E014","BATCH-0018-E015"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a complete end-of-period assessment across the entire program portfolio.","Some end-period conclusions rely on outcomes extending into 2024 or on evaluative interpretation rather than adjudicated findings."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["Evidence concerns multiple policy domains and levels of government; presidential attribution is often partial.","The shard includes favorable, adverse, and mixed records from official, international, oversight, academic, and advocacy sources; source perspective and causal limits should be preserved.","No score is assigned."]}
